gloss: take hold, grasp, seize; hold fast; be fastened, shut; (niphal) take possession; possession, holding
summary: To lay hold of and keep hold: a hand that grasps a heel, a tail, the horns of the altar or a beloved and will not let go; men who seize a fugitive; a trap that catches; and pangs and trembling that seize the fearful. What holds is also fastened: beams that hold into a wall, a door barred, a footstool fastened to a throne. The niphal is to be held fast in a land, to take possession and settle, and the noun אֲחֻזָּה is the land so held, above all the land of Canaan that Yahweh gave Abraham and his seed “for an everlasting possession” (Gen 17:8), the family holding that returned to its owner at the jubilee, and the land Ezekiel sees divided again among Israel. Arabic ʾaḫaḏa “take, seize, take possession”, with إِخَاذَةٌ “land a man takes for himself”, and the Syriac ʾeḥad of the Peshitta, “seize, hold, shut”, show the same range.

words.gloss: take hold of, grasp, hold; seize, catch; be fastened, bar; (niphal) be caught; take possession, settle
words.summary: Sixty-eight times, almost all qal. Its core is the grip that takes and keeps: Jacob's hand on Esau's heel (Gen 25:26), the bride who “held him and would not let him go” (Sng 3:4), Yahweh who holds the psalmist's right hand (Psa 73:23). The opposite is letting go (רָפָה, Sng 3:4; Ecc 7:18), and its parallel is חָזַק “hold fast” (Job 18:9). The brief's Job 23:9 אָחַז is the verb חָזָה “see”, filed here by spelling, and is left out.

stems.gloss: take hold of, grasp, hold; seize, catch; (of pangs) seize; be fastened, bar; (passive participle) taken by lot

senses.definition: To put out the hand and take hold of something, and to keep hold of it: a tail, a heel, the horns of the altar, a beard, a sword or spear, a cloak held out, a beloved; of Yahweh, to hold a man by the hand.

evidence.note: Jacob came out “and his hand אֹחֶזֶת on the heel of Esau”.
“Put out your hand וֶאֱחֹז בִּזְנָבוֹ”: Moses put out his hand and caught it, and it became a staff in his palm.
“I held him (אֲחַזְתִּיו) and would not let him go (וְלֹא אַרְפֶּנּוּ)”: to hold is the opposite of letting go.
“I am continually with you; you hold (אָחַזְתָּ) my right hand.”
“Even there your hand will lead me, and your right hand will hold me.”
Adonijah “has taken hold of the horns of the altar”.
Uzzah put out his hand to the ark of God “and took hold of it, for the oxen stumbled”; told again at 1Ch 13:9.
Joab's right hand took hold of Amasa's beard to kiss him.
“Bring the cloak that is on you and hold it”; and she held it.
“All of them holding swords, trained in war.”
Chosen men “holding spear and shield”.
“I will go up the palm tree, I will take hold of its fruit stalks.”
Samson took hold of the doors of the city gate and the two posts and pulled them up.
“My foot has held to his steps; I have kept his way and not turned aside”: holding to a way is keeping it.
“The righteous holds to his way, and the clean of hands grows stronger.”
“It is good that you take hold of this, and also from that do not let go your hand (אַל־תַּנַּח).”
The Preacher set out “to take hold of folly” to see what was good for men.
“If I sharpen my flashing sword and my hand takes hold on judgment, I will return vengeance.”
The dawn is sent “to take hold of the edges of the earth, and the wicked are shaken out of it”.
“You held my eyelids open; I was troubled and could not speak.”

senses.definition: To lay hold of a man or beast by force: a fugitive or enemy captured, a prey seized by a lion, foxes caught; of Yahweh against Job, to seize by the neck.

evidence.note: Adoni-bezek fled, “and they pursued him and seized him, and cut off his thumbs and his big toes”.
He said “Sibboleth”, “and they seized him and slaughtered him at the fords of the Jordan”.
“The Philistines seized him and gouged out his eyes … and bound him with bronze fetters.”
David: the one who brought news of Saul's death “I seized and killed at Ziklag”.
The heading: “when the Philistines seized him in Gath”.
Abner to Asahel: “seize one of the young men and take his spoil”.
“I took hold of my concubine and cut her in pieces.”
Like young lions “it growls and seizes (וְיֹאחֵז) the prey and carries it off, and none delivers”.
“Blessed is he who seizes and dashes your little ones against the rock.”
“Catch us the foxes, the little foxes that spoil the vineyards.”
“He has seized me by the neck and shattered me.”
“A trap seizes (יֹאחֵז) him by the heel; a snare holds fast (יַחֲזֵק) on him”: parallel to חָזַק.

senses.gloss: (of pangs, trembling, horror) seize, take hold of
senses.definition: Said of what comes on a man and will not let him go: anguish, trembling and pangs like a woman's in labour, horror, rage, days of affliction.

evidence.note: “The peoples have heard, they tremble; anguish (חִיל) has seized the inhabitants of Philistia.”
“Trembling seizes the mighty men of Moab.”
“Pangs and agonies will seize them; they will writhe like a woman in labour.”
“Pangs (צִירִים) have seized me, like the pangs of a woman in labour.”
“Sinners in Zion are afraid; trembling has seized the godless.”
“Will not pangs seize you like a woman in labour?”
Damascus: “trembling has seized her; anguish and pangs have taken her like a woman in labour”.
The kings who saw Zion: “trembling seized them there, anguish as of a woman in labour”.
Saul: “kill me, for agony has seized me, yet my life is still whole in me”.
“When I remember I am dismayed, and shuddering seizes my flesh.”
“Those of the east are seized with horror.”
“Days of affliction have seized me.”
“Burning rage has seized me because of the wicked who forsake your law.”

senses.gloss: be held fast, fastened; bar (a door)
senses.definition: Of building and furnishing: beams that take hold in a wall, a side building held onto the house, hangings fastened with cords; of doors, to bar them shut.

evidence.note: He made offsets round the house “so that the beams should not take hold (לְבִלְתִּי אֲחֹז) in the walls of the house”.
The side chambers came to rest on ledges “so that they should not be held (אֲחוּזִים) in the wall of the house”.
The side structure “held onto the house (וַיֶּאֱחֹז אֶת־הַבַּיִת) with cedar timbers”.
White hangings “fastened (אָחוּז) with cords of fine linen and purple to silver rings”.
“While they stand guard let them shut (יָגִיפוּ) the doors וֶאֱחֹזוּ”: and bar them; set beside shutting.

senses.definition: Of one taken out of a number: one of every fifty taken for the Levites, and a father's house drawn for each priestly line.

evidence.note: From Israel's half of the spoil “take one taken out (אֶחָד אָחֻז) of every fifty … and give them to the Levites”.
Moses took “the one taken out of every fifty”.
The priestly courses by lot: “one father's house taken (אָחֻז) for Eleazar, and one taken for Ithamar”.

stems.gloss: be caught; be settled in, take possession of (a land)

senses.definition: To be held fast by what has seized one: a ram caught in a thicket, fish in a net.

evidence.note: “A ram, behind him, caught (נֶאֱחַז) in the thicket by its horns”, offered in Isaac's place.
“Like fish taken (שֶׁנֶּאֱחָזִים) in an evil net, and birds caught (הָאֲחֻזוֹת, qal passive) in the snare, so are men snared in an evil time.”

senses.gloss: be settled in, take possession, acquire holdings
senses.definition: To be held in a land and to hold it: to settle and gain property there, as Israel in Goshen, or to take a holding among one's brothers.

evidence.note: Hamor to Jacob's sons: “the land is before you; dwell and trade in it, וְהֵאָחֲזוּ בָהּ”: acquire holdings in it.
“Israel dwelt in the land of Egypt, in the land of Goshen, וַיֵּאָחֲזוּ בָהּ, and were fruitful and multiplied greatly.”
If Gad and Reuben do not cross armed, “they shall take possession (וְנֹאחֲזוּ) among you in the land of Canaan”.
To “the land of their possession (אֲחֻזָּתָם) which they had taken possession of (נֹאחֲזוּ־בָהּ) by the mouth of Yahweh”: verb and noun together.
“Cross over to the land of the possession of Yahweh … וְהֵאָחֲזוּ in our midst.”

senses.gloss: shut in, close off (the face of)
senses.definition: Once, of God over the heavens: he closes off the face of the throne (or of the full moon, כֶּסֶה), spreading his cloud over it.

evidence.note: “מְאַחֵז פְּנֵי־כִסֵּה, spreading his cloud over it”: the cloud spread over it says how it is closed off. The Targum renders it with Aramaic אחד “lock up, hide”.

senses.definition: Once, of the footstool of Solomon's throne, fastened to it in gold.

evidence.note: “Six steps to the throne, and a footstool in gold, fastened (מָאֳחָזִים) to the throne.”

greek.gloss: take hold of, grasp; hold fast

evidence.locator: Psa.73.23, אָחַזְתָּ → ἐκράτησας; Sng.3.4, אֲחַזְתִּי → ἐκράτησα; κρατέω renders אָחַז ×12

evidence.note: Jesus “took her by the hand (ἐκράτησεν τῆς χειρὸς αὐτῆς), and the girl arose”; the Peshitta has ܐܚܕܗ ܒܐܝܕܗ, Syriac ʾeḥad.
“He who holds (ὁ κρατῶν) the seven stars in his right hand”; Peshitta ܐܚܝܕ.
“Hold fast what you have, that no one take your crown.”

evidence.locator: Gen.25.26, אֹחֶזֶת → ἐπειλημμένη; Exo.4.4, אֱחֹז → ἐπιλαβοῦ; ἐπιλαμβάνομαι renders אָחַז ×5

evidence.note: Jesus “stretched out his hand and took hold of him (ἐπελάβετο αὐτοῦ)”; Peshitta ܘܐܚܕܗ.

parallels.note: Hold fast: the trap seizes, the snare holds fast.
Anguish, the pangs of labour, as what seizes.
Shutting the doors, then barring them.

opposites.note: Let go: “I held him and would not let him go.”

words.summary: Sixty-seven tokens, nearly all of land: what is held as one's own, by Yahweh's gift, by purchase or by inheritance. It is the land given to Abraham and his seed, the field and cave he bought for a grave, the family holding of the jubilee, the cities of the Levites, and the portions of Ezekiel's land. Its parallel is נַחֲלָה “inheritance”, often joined to it (“a possession of inheritance”, Num 27:7). The brief's Gen 26:26 token is the name Ahuzzath, filed here as well (names/ahuzzath.json).

senses.gloss: possession, land held as one's own
senses.definition: Land held by a people or a man, given to them to hold: above all the land of Canaan, which Yahweh gave Abraham and his seed and later Israel “for a possession”; also Gilead for Reuben and Gad, Goshen given by Joseph, Edom's land, and for the Son, the ends of the earth.

evidence.note: “I will give to you and to your seed after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, לַאֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם, and I will be their God.”
Jacob repeats it: “I will give this land to your seed after you אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם.”
“The land of Canaan, which I give you for a possession … a house in the land of your possession.”
Moses sees from Nebo “the land of Canaan which I give to the sons of Israel for a possession”.
Reuben and Gad: “let this land be given to your servants for a possession”.
Once the land is subdued before Yahweh, “this land shall be yours for a possession before Yahweh”.
“The possession of our inheritance shall be beyond the Jordan.”
“Go to the land of your possession, which Moses gave you beyond the Jordan.”
“If the land of your possession is unclean, cross over to the land of the possession of Yahweh, where the tabernacle of Yahweh dwells.”
Joseph “gave them a possession in the land of Egypt, in the best of the land”.
The chiefs of Edom “by their dwellings in the land of their possession”.

To the Son: “Ask of me, and I will give the nations as your inheritance (נַחֲלָתֶךָ) and the ends of the earth as your possession (וַאֲחֻזָּתְךָ)”; the psalm is quoted of Jesus at Act 13:33 and Rev 2:26–27.

Stephen: God “gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot's length, but promised to give it to him for a possession (εἰς κατάσχεσιν), and to his seed after him”: the Septuagint's word for אֲחֻזָּה of Gen 17:8.

senses.definition: A man's or a family's own portion of the land, which might be sold or devoted but not lost for ever: it was redeemed by a kinsman and returned to its owner at the jubilee. A man without sons could still have his name kept by a possession given to his daughters.

evidence.note: “It shall be a jubilee for you, and you shall return each man to his possession (אֶל־אֲחֻזָּתוֹ) and each man to his family.”
“In this year of jubilee you shall return each man to his possession.”
“In all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption for the land”, following “the land is mine” (25:23).
“If your brother becomes poor and sells some of his possession, his nearest redeemer shall come and redeem.”
“In the jubilee it shall go out, and he shall return to his possession.”
The Israelite servant goes out at the jubilee “and returns to the possession of his fathers”.
“If a man consecrates to Yahweh part of the field of his possession.”
A field bought, “not of the field of his possession”.
At the jubilee the field returns to him “to whom the possession of the land belongs”.
A field devoted and not redeemed becomes the priest's possession.
Zelophehad's daughters: “Why should our father's name be taken away from his family because he had no son? Give us a possession among our father's brothers.”
“You shall surely give them a possession of inheritance (אֲחֻזַּת נַחֲלָה) among their father's brothers.”
After the high priest's death the manslayer “shall return to the land of his possession”.
After Hezekiah's cleansing “all the sons of Israel returned, each to his possession, to their cities”.
After the return, Israel, priests and Levites dwelt “each in his possession in their cities”.
“The first inhabitants who were in their possessions in their cities.”
Ephraim's “possessions and dwellings”: Bethel and its towns.
The fields and villages of Hebron given to Caleb “for his possession”.

senses.definition: The field and cave of Machpelah, which Abraham, “a stranger and sojourner”, bought from the sons of Heth: the only part of the promised land he held, and that for a grave.

evidence.note: “I am a stranger and a sojourner (גֵּר־וְתוֹשָׁב) with you; give me a possession of a grave (אֲחֻזַּת־קֶבֶר) with you, that I may bury my dead.”
“For the full price let him give it to me among you for a possession of a grave.”
“The field and the cave in it were made sure to Abraham for a possession of a grave by the sons of Heth.”
Jacob asks to be buried there, “which Abraham bought with the field … for a possession of a grave”.

senses.gloss: the Levites' holding; Yahweh the priests' possession
senses.definition: The Levites had no tribal territory: they were given cities and pasture out of Israel's possession, and these were their perpetual possession. Of the priests Yahweh says that he himself is their possession.

evidence.note: “They shall give to the Levites, from the inheritance of their possession, cities to dwell in.”
“The cities you give from the possession of the sons of Israel.”
“All the cities of the Levites in the midst of the possession of the sons of Israel were forty-eight.”
“The houses of the cities of their possession” may be redeemed at any time.
Their pasture land may not be sold, “for it is their perpetual possession (אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם)”.
Under Jeroboam “the Levites left their pasture lands and their possession and came to Judah and Jerusalem”.
“I am their inheritance; you shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession (אֲנִי אֲחֻזָּתָם).”

senses.definition: Once of persons: bondservants bought from the foreigners living in the land, who could be held and passed on as property, which an Israelite brother never could.

evidence.note: From the sojourners' families “you may buy, and they shall be your possession”.
“You may leave them to your sons after you to inherit as a possession … but over your brothers, the sons of Israel, you shall not rule with harshness.”

senses.definition: In Ezekiel's closing vision the land is measured out again: a possession for the Levites, for the city, and for the prince, who must not take the people's possession from them.

evidence.note: A portion “for the Levites, the ministers of the house, for a possession”.
“The possession of the city … for the whole house of Israel.” The brief files this token under the name Ahuzzath as well.
“It shall be his possession in Israel, and my princes shall no more oppress my people, but they shall give the land to the house of Israel by their tribes.”
The prince's gift to his sons “is their possession by inheritance”.

“The prince shall not take from the people's inheritance, thrusting them out of their possession; from his own possession he shall give his sons an inheritance, that my people be not scattered, each man from his possession.”

evidence.locator: Gen.17.8 and Gen.48.4, אֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם → κατάσχεσιν αἰώνιον; κατάσχεσις renders אֲחֻזָּה ×31

evidence.note: “He promised to give it to him for a possession (εἰς κατάσχεσιν), and to his seed after him”: Stephen's words for the promise of Gen 17:8.
The tabernacle brought in with Joshua “in the taking possession (ἐν τῇ κατασχέσει) of the nations”.

parallels.note: Inheritance: set beside it, and joined to it as “possession of inheritance”.

phrases.gloss: a possession of a grave, a burial ground
each man to his possession (of the return at the jubilee and after)

words.gloss: take hold of, seize, arrest; hold, hold fast, have; shut; (ethpeel) be seized, be held, be shut; (aphel) let out; kindle
words.summary: The Peshitta's verb for the root, about one hundred and seventy times: the Syriac form of אָחַז, with ד for the older ḏ that Hebrew writes ז. It renders κρατέω, ἐπιλαμβάνομαι, κατέχω, πιάζω, συλλαμβάνω and κλείω, the same range as the Hebrew: taking by the hand, arresting, holding fast, shutting.

stems.gloss: take hold of, seize, arrest; hold, hold fast, have; take possession; shut

senses.gloss: take hold of, take by the hand; hold
senses.definition: To take a person by the hand or take hold of him, above all Jesus taking the sick and the dead by the hand to raise them; to hold something in the hand.

evidence.note: “He went in and took her by her hand, and the girl arose.”
“He took her by the hand and raised her up, and the fever left her.”
Jesus stretched out his hand and took hold of Peter sinking.
Peter “took him by the right hand and raised him up”; the brief aligns it with Psa 73:23 and 2Sa 20:9.
“He took the blind man by the hand and led him out.”
Jer 31:32, “in the day I took them by the hand to bring them out of the land of Egypt”.
The women “took hold of his feet and worshipped him”.
“He who holds the seven stars in his right hand.”
Four angels “holding the four winds of the earth”.

senses.definition: To lay hold of a man by force: the arrest of John, of Jesus, of the apostles; and of fear and amazement that seize those who see God's works.

evidence.note: “Whomever I kiss, that is he; seize him.”
“They laid hands on Jesus and seized him.”
“Have you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs to seize me?”
“They sought to seize him, but no one laid a hand on him, because his hour had not yet come.”
Herod seized John and bound him.
The tenants seized the servants.
“Amazement seized them all, and they glorified God”: as Hebrew pangs and trembling seize.
“Fear seized them all.”
“Trembling and amazement held them.”

senses.definition: To keep hold of a teaching, a confession, a hope or what one has, and not let it go.

evidence.note: “Test all things; hold fast what is good.”
“To hold fast the hope set before us.”
“If we hold fast our confidence and the boast of our hope to the end.”
“Hold fast what you have until I come.”
“Leaving the commandment of God you hold the tradition of men.”
“Not holding fast the head.”
Those who hear the word “hold it fast and bear fruit with endurance”.

senses.definition: To take and hold as one's own: an inheritance seized, a kingdom received, all things possessed; to have.

evidence.note: The tenants: “This is the heir; come, let us kill him and seize (ܘܢܐܚܘܕ) his inheritance.”
“Since we receive (hold) a kingdom that cannot be shaken.”
“As having nothing, and yet possessing all things.”
“He who has the Son has life.”
“Let each man have his own wife.”

senses.definition: To shut a door or the sky, and to hold back: the restrainer, sins retained, eyes held from knowing him.

evidence.note: “Go into your room and shut your door, and pray to your Father in secret.”
“He who has the key of David, who opens and no one shuts, and shuts and no one opens”: Isa 22:22, whose Targum also uses אחד.
He threw him into the abyss “and shut it and sealed it over him”.
“They have power to shut the sky, that no rain fall.”
“The doors being shut where the disciples were.”
“Whose sins you retain, they are retained.”
“Their eyes were held, that they should not know him.”
“Only he who now restrains, until he is taken out of the way.”

stems.gloss: be seized, be caught, be held; be shut

senses.gloss: be seized, caught, held; be shut
senses.definition: The passive: to be caught in an act, to be held by death, to be shut.

evidence.note: God raised him up, loosing the pangs of death, “because it was not possible for him to be held by it”.
“This woman was caught in the very act of adultery.”
“Those who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the door was shut.”
“When the heaven was shut up three years and six months.”
“Immediately the doors were shut.”
“Its gates shall not be shut by day, for there shall be no night there.”

senses.definition: To make others hold: of a vineyard let out to tenants in Jesus' parable.

evidence.note: A householder planted a vineyard “and let it out (ܘܐܘܚܕܗ) to tenants”.
“He will let out the vineyard to other tenants.”

senses.definition: To make a fire take hold: twice, of a fire lit.

evidence.note: “They kindled a fire in the middle of the courtyard.”
The islanders “kindled a fire and received us all”.

words.summary: A noun of the Peshitta, the hold one has over others: the realm of Caesar, and in the doxologies the power (κράτος) ascribed to God and the Lamb.

senses.definition: Rule held over a realm, and the power ascribed to God for ever.

evidence.note: A decree from Caesar Augustus that all the people of his dominion should be registered (Greek “all the world”).
“To him be the glory and the dominion for ever and ever.”
“To him who sits on the throne and to the Lamb be blessing and honour and glory and dominion.”

words.gloss: holder; (אֲחִיד כֹּל) holder of all, the Almighty
words.summary: The participle as a noun, “holder”, chiefly in אֲחִיד כֹּל “holder of all”, the Peshitta's word for παντοκράτωρ: the God who holds all things in his grip.

senses.definition: One who holds: the rulers who hold the world, and God, who holds all things.

evidence.note: “I am the Alpha and the Omega, says the Lord God, who is and who was and who is to come, the holder of all.”
“We give thanks to you, Lord God, holder of all … because you have taken your great power and reigned.”
“Hallelujah, for the Lord our God, the holder of all, reigns.”
“Says the Lord, holder of all”: the participle of the verb, in the same phrase.
The Son, “holding all things by the word of his power”.
“Against the holders (rulers) of this world of darkness.”

cognates.gloss: take, take with the hand, take hold of; take possession of; retain, detain; seize by force, take captive; (of a tremor) seize; (أَخِيذٌ) captive
cognates.note: The whole range of the Hebrew in one verb: the hand's grip, the capture, the fear that seizes, and taking land as one's own. Arabic shows ḫ behind ח and ḏ behind ז.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 28, art. أخذ, أَخَذَ (n346)
evidence.note: “He took; he took with his hand; he took hold of”; “He took a thing to, or for, himself; took possession of it; got, or acquired, it; syn. حَازَ”; “He retained; he detained”; “He, or it, took by force; or seized”; “He took captive”; أَخَذَتْهُ رِعْدَةٌ “A tremour seized … him”.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 30, art. أخذ, أَخِيذٌ (n362)
evidence.note: “Taken; taken with the hand … A captive.”
From Proto-Semitic *ʔaḫaḏ-; cognate with Hebrew אָחַז, Aramaic ܐܚܕ, Sabaean ʾḫḏ.

cognates.gloss: land which a man takes for himself (and brings into cultivation); land granted to one
cognates.note: A noun of the same verb for land taken and held as one's own: the closest match to אֲחֻזָּה, the land held by gift or grant.

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 30, art. أخذ, إِخَاذَةٌ (n363)
evidence.note: “Land which a man, or a Sultán, takes for himself; as also إِخَاذٌ: or land which a man takes for himself, and brings into a state of cultivation after its having been waste … and land which the Imám gives to one.”

evidence.locator: Book I, p. 30, art. أخذ, إِخَاذٌ (n361)
evidence.note: “إِخَاذَةٌ … land of which a man takes possession for himself.”

cognates.gloss: take, seize, grasp; marry; mount, plate, inlay (in precious metal); learn; (Š) kindle, set fire to
cognates.note: Akkadian keeps ḫ but writes z for both z and ḏ. Its “mount, inlay in precious metal” is the fastening of 2Ch 9:18, a footstool fastened to the throne in gold, and its “kindle” the Syriac aphel.

evidence.note: 797 instances; meanings include “take”, “seize”, “grasp”, “marry”, “mount, plate, inlay”, “kindle”, “set fire to”.

cognates.gloss: close (a door), lock up; seize, capture; (pass. part.) locked up; holding; (Af.) seize; (Ithpe.) be seized, be locked up
cognates.note: Jewish Aramaic of the Targums and Talmud. The Targum renders the piel of Job 26:9 with its passive participle מְאַחַד “locked up, hidden”, and the qal of Psa 73:23 with the Af. “seize”. Aramaic ד shows ḏ behind ז.

evidence.locator: s.v. אֲחַד (ch.) (A00996), citing Targ. Is. XXII, 22; Snh. 26a; Targ. Josh. VI, 1; Targ. Job XXVI, 9 (Pa. part. pass. מְאַחַד); Targ. Ps. LXXIII, 23 (Af.); Targ. Ez. XIX, 4 (Ithpe.); Ḥull. 52b
evidence.note: “(corresp. to h. סגר a. תפש; cmp. h. אחז) to close (the door), to lock up; to seize, capture.”
“to hold, take, seize; to shut, close”; from Proto-Semitic *ʔaḫaḏ.

cognates.note: Ugaritic shows ḫ behind ח; it is also written 𐎀𐎃𐎏 ảḫḏ.

evidence.locator: x000003280, ʾḫd, collect (V), forms ʾaḫd, ʾiḫd, ʾiḫdn, ʾuḫd, yʾiḫd
Ugaritic 𐎀𐎃𐎄 (ảḫd), verb; 𐎀𐎃𐎏 (ảḫḏ), alternative form
evidence.note: “to collect, to take (back), grasp, seize, hold”.

cognates.gloss: take hold of, seize, apprehend; (of fear, pain) seize; capture; hold, hold fast; occupy, possess, rule
cognates.note: Geʿez keeps ḫ behind ח (it writes z for both z and ḏ). Its “occupy, possess, rule” matches the niphal and the noun, and its participle “holder of all” is the Syriac אֲחִיד כֹּל.

evidence.note: “1) prehendere, comprehendere, apprehendere … timor, terror, calamitas, dolor, morbus prehendit i. e. corripit alqm: Ex. 15, 14. 15 … b) comprehendere, deprehendere alqm captivum … c) capere … 2) prehensum tenere, tenere: Gen. 25, 26 … c) occupare, potiri, possidere, dominari, obtinere.”
“to take, catch”; from Proto-Semitic *ʔḫḏ.

cognates.gloss: (Sabaic) capture, take in war; (n.) prisoner, prize taken in war
cognates.note: Old South Arabian keeps both ḫ and ḏ apart, as Arabic does.

evidence.note: “CAPTURE, TAKE IN WAR; EXACT PAYMENT FROM [Ar ʾaḫaḏa ‘take, seize’]”, J560/2 “and the soldiers captured the territory”; noun “PRISONER or PRIZE TAKEN IN WAR”.
“to take, seize”.

cognates.note: Moabite, in Mesha's own inscription: the same spelling as the Hebrew, of taking Nebo from Israel.

evidence.note: ויאמר לי כמש לכ אחז את נבה על ישראל, “And Kemôš said unto me, Go, seize Neḇôh against Yisrāʾēl.”

doctrine.statement: Yahweh said to Abraham, “all the land which you see, to you I will give it and to your seed for ever” (Gen 13:15), and again, “I will give to you and to your seed after you the land of your sojournings, all the land of Canaan, for an everlasting possession (לַאֲחֻזַּת עוֹלָם)” (Gen 17:8); Jacob repeated it to Joseph (Gen 48:4). Yet Abraham called himself “a stranger and a sojourner” in that land, and the only possession he ever held in it was “a possession of a grave”, the cave of Machpelah, which he bought to bury Sarah and in which he, Isaac and Jacob were buried (Gen 23:4, 20; 49:30; 50:13). Stephen says the same: God “gave him no inheritance in it, not even a foot's length, but promised to give it to him for a possession, and to his seed after him” (Act 7:5). Hebrews adds that Abraham, Isaac and Jacob dwelt in the land of promise as strangers, “these all died in faith, not having received the promises”, and “not having received the promise, God having provided something better for us, that apart from us they should not be made perfect” (Heb 11:9, 13, 39–40). The seed to whom the promise was made is Christ, and those who are Christ's are Abraham's seed and heirs according to the promise (Gal 3:16, 29). Jesus said many “will recline with Abraham, Isaac and Jacob in the kingdom” (Mat 8:11). From the verses: the promise was of a land that could be walked and seen, made to Abraham himself and not only to his descendants; he died without it, so it remains to be given, and it can be given to him only when he is raised from the dead, together with Christ's people, in the kingdom at Christ's return.

The law of the jubilee says, “the land shall not be sold for ever, for the land is mine; you are strangers and sojourners with me”, and at once, “in all the land of your possession you shall grant redemption for the land” (Lev 25:23–24). Each family's possession could be sold only until the jubilee, when “each man shall return to his possession” (Lev 25:10, 13, 28); a poor man's possession was to be redeemed by his nearest kinsman (Lev 25:25); and Zelophehad's daughters were given a possession so that their father's name should not be taken away (Num 27:4, 7). Of the priests Yahweh says, “you shall give them no possession in Israel; I am their possession” (Ezk 44:28). From the verses: Israel held its land as a grant from its owner, Yahweh, on his terms; a possession was never lost for ever but came back to its family, and those who served him had Yahweh himself for their holding.

Ezekiel's last vision measures the land out again. Yahweh shows him “the place of my throne … where I will dwell in the midst of the sons of Israel for ever” (Ezk 43:7); the Levites, the city and the prince each have their possession; the prince “shall not take from the people's inheritance, thrusting them out of their possession”, and “my princes shall no more oppress my people, but they shall give the land to the house of Israel by their tribes” (Ezk 45:5–8; 46:18; 48:20–22). Earlier in the book Yahweh had said that Israel “shall dwell in the land that I gave to Jacob my servant … for ever, and David my servant shall be their prince for ever” (Ezk 37:25). The second psalm gives the Son “the nations for your inheritance and the ends of the earth for your possession (אֲחֻזָּתְךָ)” (Psa 2:8), and the New Testament reads the psalm of Jesus (Act 13:33) and promises his faithful a share in his rule over the nations (Rev 2:26–27). From the verses: the land promised as a possession is given again, under a king of David's line, with Yahweh dwelling among his people; it is the kingdom of God on the earth, when Christ holds the nations as his possession.

note: Drafted 2026-11-19. Keys: a.cl.aa (verb, 68 tokens) and a.cl.ac (noun, 67). Names in names/: ahaz (a.cl.ab), ahaziah (a.cl.ad, with Ahzai of Neh 11:13), jehoahaz (e.az.ah, e.az.be, filed by BDB under הוה), ahuzzath (a.cl.af), ahuzzam (a.cl.ae). The brief's a.cl.af (Ahuzzath) also counts Ezk 45:6, the noun, and a.cl.ac also counts Gen 26:26, the name; both double counts are left as the corpus files them. Left out: Job 23:9 אָחַז, analysed as חָזָה “see”; h.bt.ad יַחְזֵרָה (Jahzerah, 1Ch 9:12, zero tokens), which BDB cross-refers to אֲחַזְיָהוּ as the same man as Ahzai but which is spelled with ר and not this root; not written. Biblical Aramaic has no word of this root: Dan 5:12 אֲחִידָן “riddles” is the root of Hebrew חִידָה. The Peshitta's root is SEDRA root 56 (אחד, AKD): lexemes 71 AKD verb (Greek links κρατέω ×41, ἐπιλαμβάνω ×12, κατέχω ×12, κλείω ×11, πιάζω ×6, συλλαμβάνω ×5), 70 AOKDNA “dominion; possession; sovereignty” (κράτος ×4), 3021 AK;DA “holder; closed” (παντοκράτωρ ×9), 72 AK;D-CL “Lord of all” (no tokens). The echad entry's note already says the brief's Peshitta אחד belongs here. Stems of the Syriac verb assigned from the vocalised forms in data/haqor.db (אֵתּתּחֵד etc. ethpeel, אַוחֵד aphel); SEDRA's form codes not checked. Lane's p. 28 article also gives أَخَذَهُ بِذَنْبِهِ “punished him for his sin”, not used. Dillmann read from the OCR only (column from the running numbers 764/766/769); not checked against the scan. Biella pages from the OCR's page breaks. DULAT (Ugaritic), Leslau 1987 (Geʿez), CAD A/1 (aḫāzu) not consulted. Mesha line 20 may have ואחזה (“and I took it”) too; not checked. Open questions: (1) the piel of Job 26:9: “closes off” (with the Targum and Syriac “shut”) or “covers” the face of the throne/full moon; (2) the qal passive participle of Num 31:30 and 1Ch 24:6 (“taken out”, by lot?) has no cognate checked; (3) doctrine kingdom-of-god reads Ezk 40–48 as the future kingdom and Psa 2:8 as Christ's; (4) Hebrew citations in notes were checked against MACULA's word forms only where aligned.
